title.zh: 卷174 表十四 大学士年表一
title.en: Volume 174 Tables 14: Grand Secretaries Chronological Table 1
title.raw: 卷174 表十四 大学士年表一

sentences.zh: 大學士年表一 清大學士，沿明舊名，例稱政府，實則國初有議政處以掣其柄，雍正以後，承旨寄信有軍機處，內閣宰輔，名存而已。

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries Chronological Table 1: Qing Grand Secretaries followed the old Ming title and were commonly called the government; in fact at the founding of the state the Council of Princes held back their power; after Yongzheng, receiving and drafting imperial orders was entrusted to the Grand Council, and the Inner Cabinet chancellors existed in name only.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries Chronological Table 1. Qing Grand Secretaries kept the Ming title and were routinely called "the government," yet at the dynasty's founding the Council of Princes held the real levers of power; after Yongzheng, drafting and relaying imperial orders passed to the Grand Council, and the Inner Cabinet's chief ministers were grand councilors in name alone.

sentences.zh: 新唐、元史表宰相者，備列三公。

translations.literal: In the tables of chancellors in the New Tang History and Yuan History, all three dukes are fully listed.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor tables in the New Tang History and the Yuan History list all three ranks of duke in full.

sentences.zh: 清大學士滿、漢兩途，勛高位極，乃以相授。

translations.literal: Qing Grand Secretaries had Manchu and Han paths; only those of highest merit and rank received the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: Qing Grand Secretaries were drawn from both Manchu and Han routes; only men of the highest merit and rank received the title of chancellor.

translations.literal: The Inner Cabinet's actual power fell far short of that under the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: The Inner Cabinet's real authority fell far short of what it had been under the Ming.

translations.literal: Yet in rank they all headed the civil service class.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in official rank they still headed the civil service roster.

sentences.zh: 任軍機者，自親王外，其領袖者必大學士，唐、元三公尚不及也。

translations.literal: Among those who served in the Grand Council, apart from imperial princes, the leaders had to be Grand Secretaries—a standing that even the three dukes of Tang and Yuan did not reach.
translations.idiomatic: Among those who served on the Grand Council, apart from imperial princes, the leaders had to be Grand Secretaries—a standing that even the three dukes of Tang and Yuan had not attained.
